In mathematics,  '''Dolgachev surfaces''' are certain [[simply connected space|simply connected]] [[elliptic surface]]s, introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Igor|last=Dolgachev|authorlink=Igor Dolgachev|year=1981}}. They can be used to give examples of an infinite family of [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] simply connected [[compact space|compact]] [[4-manifold]]s, no two of which are [[diffeomorphism|diffeomorphic]].

==Properties==
The [[blowing up|blowup]] <math>X_0</math> of the [[projective plane]] in 9 points can be realized as an elliptic fibration all of whose fibers are irreducible. A Dolgachev surface <math>X_q</math> is given by applying [[logarithmic transformation]]s of orders 2 and ''q'' to two smooth fibers  for some <math>q\ge 3</math>.

The Dolgachev surfaces are simply connected, and the bilinear form on the second [[cohomology group]] is odd of [[signature (topology)|signature]] <math>(1,9)</math> (so it is the [[unimodular lattice]] <math>I_{1,9}</math>). The [[geometric genus]] <math>p_g</math> is 0 and the [[Kodaira dimension]] is&nbsp;1.

{{harvs|txt|first=Simon|last=Donaldson|authorlink=Simon Donaldson|year=1987}} found the first examples of simply-connected homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic 4-manifolds  <math>X_0</math> and <math>X_3</math>.  More generally the surfaces <math>X_q</math> and <math>X_r</math> are always homeomorphic, but  are not  diffeomorphic unless <math>q=r</math>.

{{harvs|txt|first=Selman|last=Akbulut|authorlink=Selman Akbulut|year=2012}} showed that the Dolgachev surface <math>X_3</math> has a [[handlebody decomposition]] without 1- and 3-handles.

== Detection of exotic smooth structures ==
According to [[Freedman classification|Freedman's classification]], a simply connected oriented closed [[Topological manifold|topological]] 4-manifold with [[Intersection form of a 4-manifold|intersection form]] <math>
[+1]\oplus 9[-1]
</math> is homeomorphic to <math>
\mathbb{C}P^2\# 9\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}
</math>. Any such smooth manifold with a non-vanishing [[Seiberg–Witten invariants|Seiberg–Witten invariant]] has an exotic smooth structure since <math>
\mathbb{C}P^2\# 9\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}
</math> with the induced smooth structure allows a [[Riemannian manifold|Riemannian metric]] of positive [[scalar curvature]] (psc metric) and therefore has only vanishing Seiberg–Witten invariants.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Salamon |first=Dietmar |author-link=Dietmar Salamon |url=https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/~a019210/Salamon_Spin%20geometry%20and%20SW%20invariants.pdf |title=Spin Geometry and Seiberg-Witten invariants |date=1999 |at=Crl. 2.19 (p. 49), Prop. 7.32 (p. 258) |language=en}}</ref>
